name: core-behaviors
description: The core's behaviors with no extension linked (D10, D16): an engine with only its own behaviors and the core meta-schema runs the documents the core binary builds in the CLI smoke: fixture-behaviors-json, whose type composes Workflow, Comments and Revisions, fixture-cross-instance-json, whose tasks wait on tasks and documents and link to both and to the project every create gives, fixture-rollups-json, whose projects roll their tasks up, fixture-search-json, whose notes are searched, fixture-reactions-json, whose projects start, finish and fail their parent, fixture-variants-json, whose steps keep their kind and hold a result of the kind's shape, fixture-branches-json, whose recipes are version graphs, and fixture-staterules-json, whose invoices need and keep fields by their status, and fixture-approvals-json, whose expense claims wait for sign-offs, fixture-numbering-json, whose invoices are numbered per project and per year, and fixture-timers-json, whose support requests are escalated or resolved when nobody moves them in time. They register when the engine opens, under names no deployment can take.

s1.name: Workflow
s1.description: A state machine on the instance: a status that starts in the initial state and changes only through transition, along a transition the config lists. A transition may name a permission the caller must hold. A state that no transition leaves is terminal, and a terminal state has an outcome: success, failure or neutral, success unless the config says otherwise. Other instances' blockers, rollups and reactions read it.

initial.description: The state a new instance starts in; the first of states when absent.

outcomes.description: The outcome of each terminal state it names: success, failure or neutral. A terminal state it does not name is a success. Each key is a terminal state of states.

states.description: Every state an instance can be in.

transitions.description: The moves the status may make. A state that no transition leaves is terminal.

from.description: The state the instance is in.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to make this transition. Absent, any caller who may write the instance can.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The state the instance is in.

fields.name: enteredAt
fields.description: When the status last changed, in epoch milliseconds: the create's time, then each transition's. Absent on an instance created before Workflow kept it, until its next transition.

operations.name: transition
operations.description: Moves the instance to another state along a transition the config lists. A transition that names a permission needs a caller who holds it.

from.description: The state the instance was in.

to.description: The state it is in now.

vetoes.description: The instance is already in the state the transition names.
The instance is in a terminal state: no transition leaves it.
No transition of the config leads from the instance's state to the one named.
The instance has no status to move from.

s7.name: Search
s7.description: Full-text search over the instance's own text fields, which the config names, and with vectors in the config, vector search over embeddings an outside embedder computes from the same text. The index is kept in the transaction of each create, update and delete; an embedder pulls the instances whose text changed since their vector was computed (staleEmbeddings) and settles their vectors back (settleEmbeddings). The schema-level search returns the matching ids in rank order, by the text, by a vector the caller gives, or by both fused, from the instances of the caller's namespace only, and similar returns the instances nearest to one, or to a draft's text.

fields.description: The type's own top-level fields to index, by JSON key, each a string or a scalar whose values are strings; at most 16. Their order is the order a snippet's field is chosen in when two match equally, and the order an embedder's text joins them in.

vectors.description: Keeps a vector per instance, which an outside embedder computes from the indexed fields' text, for vector and hybrid search. A version that changes the model or the dimensions makes every vector stale.

dimensions.description: How many numbers a vector holds.

model.description: A label for the embedding model the vectors come from, which the engine only compares: an embedder computes with it, and a query vector may name it.

permission.description: The permission an embedder needs to settle vectors.

weights.description: A weight per indexed field, which multiplies that field's part of a match's score; 1 for a field it does not name.

operations.name: search
operations.description: Searches the schema's instances in the caller's namespace and returns the matching ids, best match first, one page at a time: by query, by vector, or by both, whose rankings are fused. A query is plain words by default: an instance matches when its indexed fields hold every word, and quotes and operators in the query are text. With syntax fts5 the query is an SQLite FTS5 expression (phrases, AND, OR, NOT, NEAR, prefix*), without column filters. A vector, computed with the config's model from the text to search for, ranks the instances whose vectors are settled by cosine similarity. With a vector, each hit says how it matched.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

query.description: What to search for, as text.

syntax.description: How to read the query: words (the default), each word as text, or fts5, an SQLite FTS5 expression.

vector.description: The vector to search for: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

field.description: The indexed field the snippet is from.

rank.description: The instance's place in the ranking, from 1 for the best match, across pages.

score.description: With a vector: the fused score, the sum of 1 / (60 + its place) over the rankings it is in, which orders the hits.

snippet.description: A few words of that field around its matches, in parts; each part says whether it is a match.

text.description: With a vector: its place in the full-text ranking, when the query matched it.

vector.description: With a vector: its place in the vector ranking and the cosine similarity of its vector to the one searched for, when its vector is settled and ranks.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: similar
operations.description: Lists the instances nearest to an existing one, leaving it out: by its own indexed text and, once its vector is settled, by its vector, the two rankings fused, each hit saying how it matched. Given text in place of an id, the text of an instance not yet created, it ranks the same way by that text and the vector given with it, if any. Call it before creating an instance, to find near-duplicates to reuse or link instead.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

id.description: The instance whose neighbours to list.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

text.description: In place of id, the text of an instance not yet created: its indexed fields that hold more than whitespace, in the config's order, joined by a blank line, as an embedder is given an instance's.

vector.description: With text, the text's vector: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

embedded.description: Whether a vector ranked: the instance's, once it is settled, or the one given with text.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: staleEmbeddings
operations.description: Lists the instances whose vector is missing or stale, in the order they were first indexed: each one's id, the text to compute its vector from (its indexed fields, joined by a blank line) and the hash of that text and the model, which a settle presents. Needs vectors in the config.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

dimensions.description: How many numbers each vector holds.

sourceHash.description: The hash of the text and the model, which the settle presents.

text.description: The text to compute the vector from.

model.description: The model to compute the vectors with.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: settleEmbeddings
operations.description: Stores the vectors an embedder computed from the text staleEmbeddings returned, each with the hash it returned with it. An item whose instance is gone, or whose text or model changed since, is skipped. A vector of the wrong dimensions, all zeros, or with a value a 32-bit float cannot hold refuses the whole batch. Needs vectors in the config and the permission it names. Appends no event: a vector is derived from text the log records, and no read of an instance shows it.

sourceHash.description: The hash staleEmbeddings returned with the text.

skipped.description: The items not stored: moved, the text or the model changed since the hash was read, so pull the instance again; not_found, the namespace has no such instance.

s13.name: Links
s13.description: Named links from the instance to instances of the schemas its config names, set by link or given at create: each holds one target, or with many a list of them. A pinned link records the target's revision (its schema composes Revisions) or its release (its schema composes Branches), and reports the target's latest beside it and whether the target has moved past it. A required link is given at create, can be moved to another target but not unlinked, and the delete of its target is refused; a required many-valued link keeps at least one target, and only its last target's delete is refused. A deleted target leaves every link that holds it.

many.description: The link holds a list of targets, in the order they were linked, rather than one.

max.description: For a many-valued link, the most targets it holds, from 1 to 100.

pinned.description: What the link records of the target, reporting the target's latest beside it and whether the target has moved past it: true or revision, its revision, whose schema must compose Revisions; release, its release, whose schema must compose Branches; false or absent, nothing.

required.description: Every create gives the link, which can then be moved to another target but not unlinked, and the delete of its target is refused. A many-valued link holds at least one target, and only the delete of its last is refused.

schema.description: The schema of the instance the link points at.

links.description: The links an instance may hold, by name: camelCase, at most 64 characters.

additionalProperties.description: The target: its id, or an object with its id and, for a pinned link, the revision or the release to record; for a many-valued link, a list of them, each target once.

items.description: One target: its id, or an object with its id and, for a pinned link, the revision or the release to record.

release.description: For a link pinned to a release, the target's release to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

revision.description: For a link pinned to a revision, the target's revision to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

release.description: For a link pinned to a release, the target's release to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

revision.description: For a link pinned to a revision, the target's revision to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

createParamsSchema.description: The links the instance holds from its create, by name, each held to link's rules. Every required link is given here.

fields.name: targets
fields.description: The links the instance holds, by name: each target's schema and id, and for a pinned link the revision or the release it records, the target's latest and whether the target has moved past it; for a many-valued link, a list of them in the order they were linked. Absent when the instance holds none.

operations.name: link
operations.description: Points a link at an instance of its schema, replacing the target it had; a many-valued link adds the instance to its list, or pins again one it holds. A pinned link records the target's latest revision or release, or the one given.

name.description: The link's name in the config.

release.description: For a link pinned to a release, the target's release to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

revision.description: For a link pinned to a revision, the target's revision to record, one it has had; its latest when absent.

release.description: The target's release a link pinned to a release records.

revision.description: The target's revision a link pinned to a revision records.

operations.name: unlink
operations.description: Clears an optional link, or removes one target of a many-valued link. A required link cannot be unlinked, only moved, and a required many-valued link keeps at least one target.

id.description: The target to remove, which a many-valued link needs; for a link that holds one target, the one it must hold.

name.description: The link's name in the config.

operations.name: listLinked
operations.description: Lists the instances of this schema whose link points at an instance, in the order the links were made, one page at a time; for a pinned link, with the revision or the release each records, the target's latest and whether the target has moved past it.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

name.description: The link's name in the config.

stale.description: Only the pinned links whose target has moved past the revision or the release they record.

id.description: The id of the instance that holds the link.

latest.description: The target's latest revision or release, of the kind the link pins.

release.description: The target's release a link pinned to a release records.

revision.description: The target's revision a link pinned to a revision records.

stale.description: Whether the target has moved past the one the link records.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

declaration.name: Comments
declaration.description: Comments on the instance, each a reply to another or not. A caller who may write the instance adds one; a caller who may read it lists them. Deleting the instance deletes its comments.

fields.name: commentCount
fields.description: How many comments the instance has.

operations.name: comment
operations.description: Adds a comment to the instance, or a reply to one of its comments.

replyTo.description: The id of the instance's comment this one replies to.

createdBy.description: The subject of the caller who added it.

id.description: The comment's number on the instance: 1, 2, 3, ...

replyTo.description: The id of the comment it replies to.

operations.name: listComments
operations.description: Lists the instance's comments, oldest first, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many comments; 50 when absent.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

declaration.name: Revisions
declaration.description: Immutable revisions of the instance's own fields: one when it is created and one each time they change, numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., read a page at a time or one by its number. With review in its config, a caller can propose a change as a merge patch, citing instances as evidence, and a caller who holds the review permission approves it, which applies the patch as an update, or rejects it; pendingProposals counts the proposals waiting. Deleting the instance deletes its revisions and proposals.

review.description: Turns on the review step: propose, approve, reject and listProposals.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to approve or reject a proposal.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: The number of the instance's latest revision.

fields.name: pendingProposals
fields.description: With review in the config, how many of the instance's proposals are pending; absent without review.

operations.name: listRevisions
operations.description: Lists the instance's revisions, oldest first, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many revisions; 50 when absent.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: getRevision
operations.description: Reads one of the instance's revisions by its number: the own fields as that change left them. A number the instance has not reached is not_found.

operations.name: propose
operations.description: Proposes a change to the instance's own fields as a JSON merge patch, for a reviewer to approve or reject. The patch must change the instance and leave it valid; nothing changes until a reviewer approves it.

evidence.description: Instances the proposal cites, for the reviewer: each one must exist and the proposer must be able to read its schema, and a revision must be one it has had, of a schema that composes Revisions. They are kept as given; a later change of an instance cited leaves them as they are.

revision.description: The revision of it the proposal rests on.

schema.description: The schema of the instance cited.

patch.description: A JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) of the instance's own fields.

base.description: The instance's revision when it was proposed.

id.description: The proposal's number on the instance: 1, 2, 3, ...

operations.name: approve
operations.description: Approves a pending proposal: applies its patch to the instance as an update, whose checks run, and records the revision it makes. Needs the review permission.

proposal.description: The id of the pending proposal.

revision.description: The instance's revision after the approval.

operations.name: reject
operations.description: Rejects a pending proposal; the instance does not change. Needs the review permission.

proposal.description: The id of the pending proposal.

operations.name: listProposals
operations.description: Lists the instance's proposals, oldest first, one page at a time; with state, only those in it.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many proposals; 50 when absent.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

vetoes.description: propose, approve, reject or listProposals on a type whose Revisions config sets no review.
approve or reject of a proposal that is no longer pending.

declaration.name: Dependencies
declaration.description: Blockers between instances. A blocker is finished once its status is a terminal state of its own schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts, a success by default. An instance is blocked while a blocker is not finished, and a transition of its own Workflow into a gated state waits until none blocks it. A blocker is an instance of the type's own schema, or of a schema the config lists, that composes Workflow; an edge that would close a cycle is refused. A create may give its blockers. Deleting a blocker removes its edges.

gatedStates.description: The states of the type's Workflow that a transition into waits for every blocker to finish; every terminal state when absent.

satisfiedBy.description: The outcomes of a blocker's terminal state that finish it; success when absent. A blocker in a terminal state whose outcome the list lacks blocks until it is removed.

schemas.description: The schemas whose instances may block this type's, each composing Workflow; the type's own schema when absent.

blockers.description: The instance's blockers from its create, each held to addBlocker's rules.

schema.description: The blocker's schema; the instance's own when absent.

fields.name: blocked
fields.description: Whether a blocker is not finished: its status is not a terminal state of its schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts.

operations.name: addBlocker
operations.description: Makes another instance block this one. It must be of the type's own schema or one the config lists, exist, and not be blocked by this instance, directly or through others. An instance in a gated state that is terminal takes no blocker that is not finished.

schema.description: The blocker's schema; the instance's own when absent.

open.description: Whether it is not finished, so it blocks: its status is not a terminal state of its schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts.

operations.name: removeBlocker
operations.description: Stops another instance from blocking this one.

schema.description: The blocker's schema; the instance's own when absent.

operations.name: listBlockers
operations.description: Lists the instance's blockers in the order they were added, one page at a time, with each one's status and whether it blocks.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many blockers; 50 when absent.

open.description: Whether it is not finished, so it blocks: its status is not a terminal state of its schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: listDependents
operations.description: Lists the instances this one blocks, of every schema the caller may read, in the order they were added, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many dependents; 50 when absent. A page holds fewer when the caller may not read some of their schemas.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

declaration.name: Rollups
declaration.description: Values derived from the instances that point at this one through a link of their schema's Links config: how many there are, how many hold each value of a field, the sum, least or greatest of a numeric field, a field's value on the one created last, and whether every one or some one is in a terminal state of its schema's Workflow, optionally one with a listed outcome. A value is computed when the instance is read, as the caller, from at most 500 linked instances; a rollup over more has none. A rollup of every or some one may gate states of the type's Workflow: a transition into one waits until the rollup holds.

field.description: For countBy, a string, enum or boolean field of the linked instances, or status when their schema composes Workflow; for sum, min and max, a numeric field; for latest, any field of theirs, or status when their schema composes Workflow.

function.description: count: how many instances point here. countBy: how many hold each value of field. sum, min, max: of the numeric field. latest: field's value on the instance created last, the greater id on a tie. all, any: whether every one, or some one, is in a terminal state of its schema's Workflow, with an outcome outcomes lists when it is given.

gatedStates.description: For all and any, the states of the type's Workflow that a transition into waits for the rollup to hold.

link.description: The link of that schema's Links config that points at this schema.

outcomes.description: For all and any, the outcomes a linked instance's terminal state must have to count; every outcome when absent.

schema.description: The schema whose instances point at this one; it composes Links.

rollups.description: The rollups, by name: camelCase, at most 64 characters.

fields.name: values
fields.description: Each rollup's value, by name, computed when the instance is read: a count, counts by value, a number, a field's value, or a boolean. A rollup whose link holds more than 500 instances is {"over": true} instead; a min or max with no value to compare, and a latest whose instance holds none, is absent.

vetoes.description: A Workflow transition into a state an all or any rollup gates while the rollup does not hold, or has no value past 500 linked instances; details names the rollup and counts the linked instances.

declaration.name: Approvals
declaration.description: Sign-offs that gate states of the type's Workflow. A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, waits until as many distinct principals holding the gate's permission as its count have signed off; the instance's creator cannot sign unless the gate allows it. A change of the instance's own fields consumes every gate's sign-offs, unless the config keeps them, and entering a gated state consumes that gate's, so a return to it signs again. Consumed sign-offs stay listed. Deleting the instance deletes its sign-offs.

count.description: How many distinct principals must sign off before a transition into the state.

excludeCreator.description: Whether the principal who created the instance is refused a sign-off; true when absent.

from.description: The states of the type's Workflow a transition from is gated; every state when absent.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to sign off.

gates.description: The gates, by the state of the type's Workflow each gates.

resetOnChange.description: Whether a change of the instance's own fields, an update or an operation's, consumes every gate's sign-offs; true when absent.

fields.name: gates
fields.description: The sign-offs not yet consumed, by gated state: { <state>: { signedBy } }, each subject that signed, in the order they signed; a gate with none is absent.

operations.name: signOff
operations.description: Signs off on the instance for a gated state, as the caller. Needs the gate's permission; refused for the instance's creator unless the gate allows it, while the instance is in the state, and for a caller whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed.

state.description: The gated state to sign off for.

resultSchema.description: The sign-off, with the gate's sign-offs after it and the count it needs.

signedBy.description: Every subject whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed, in the order they signed.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

operations.name: withdrawSignOff
operations.description: Withdraws the caller's sign-off for a gated state, one not yet consumed.

state.description: The gated state whose sign-off to withdraw.

at.description: When it was signed, in epoch milliseconds.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

operations.name: listSignOffs
operations.description: Lists the instance's sign-offs, oldest first, one page at a time, the consumed ones included; with state, only those for it.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many sign-offs; 50 when absent.

consumedAt.description: When a change of the own fields, entering the state or a new version without its gate consumed it; absent while it counts.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

vetoes.description: A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, with fewer sign-offs than its count; details give the state, the count required and the sign-offs it has.
signOff by a caller whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed.
signOff by the principal who created the instance, on a gate that excludes the creator.
signOff while the instance is in the gated state.
signOff or withdrawSignOff for a state the config does not gate.
withdrawSignOff by a caller with no sign-off for the state that is not yet consumed.

declaration.name: Timers
declaration.description: Named deadlines on the instance, each due a time after it starts: at the create, each time the status of the type's Workflow enters a state, or at the time a date-time field of the instance holds, before it with a negative offset. A due deadline fires once: it is marked fired and can move the status, from the state it starts in unless the config names others, whatever the move meets. A change of the status can cancel a pending deadline, and a field deadline moves with its field. The engine's runner fires the due deadlines every sweepMs; a caller with the config's permission resets or snoozes one. A deadline that names a state needs Workflow on the type.

afterMs.description: How long after its start the deadline is due, in milliseconds; 0 when absent. Negative, before its start, for a field start alone.

start.description: What the deadline starts from: the instance's create ({ create: true }), each entry of the status into a state of the type's Workflow ({ enters }), or the time an own date-time field holds ({ field }), which moves the deadline when it changes and cancels it when it is cleared.

enters.description: A state of the type's Workflow; the deadline starts again at each entry into it.

field.description: An own field of the type, by JSON key, whose values are date-times.

then.description: Moves the status of the type's Workflow, through its transition, when the deadline fires while the status is one of from.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other it stays. When absent, the state the deadline starts in: its enters state, or the Workflow's initial state for a create start. A field start names them.

until.description: Cancels the deadline while it is pending once a change leaves the status out of the state it starts in ({ leaves }) or in one of the states given ({ enters }). Needs Workflow on the type.

leaves.description: The state the deadline starts in: its enters state, or the Workflow's initial state for a create start.

enters.description: States of the type's Workflow, none of them the state the deadline starts in.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to reset or snooze a deadline; nobody may when absent.

sweepMs.description: How often the engine's runner fires the due deadlines, in milliseconds; 5000 when absent.

fields.name: deadlines
fields.description: Each started deadline, by name: { dueAt, fired, firedAt?, outcome? }, when it is due, in epoch milliseconds, whether it has fired and when, and what its then met: moved, skipped (the status was not one it moves from), vetoed or forbidden. A deadline not started, or cancelled, is absent. Nothing in it follows the clock: a deadline is overdue while it has not fired and its dueAt has passed.

operations.name: fireTimer
operations.description: Fires a deadline that is due and has not fired: marks it fired and moves the status by its then, recording the outcome; a veto or a missing permission the move meets leaves the status as it is and the deadline fired. A deadline whose until holds is cancelled instead. On a deadline not due, fired already or not started it changes nothing. Any principal who may write the instance may call it; the engine's runner calls it on every due deadline, every sweepMs.

fired.description: Whether this call fired the deadline.

outcome.description: When it fired a deadline with then: what the move met.

operations.name: resetTimer
operations.description: Starts a deadline again from what it starts from now, the create, the status's entry into its state or its field's value, so it is due afterMs after it and not fired: a snooze or a fire is undone. Needs the config's permission; refused for a deadline with nothing to start from now, or whose until holds.

dueAt.description: When it is due, in epoch milliseconds.

operations.name: snoozeTimer
operations.description: Moves a started deadline's due time to dueAt, and a fired one fires again then. A later write keeps it, until what the deadline starts from changes. Needs the config's permission; refused for a deadline not started, cancelled, or whose until holds.

dueAt.description: When it is due, in epoch milliseconds.
When it is due, in epoch milliseconds.

vetoes.description: fireTimer, resetTimer or snoozeTimer of a deadline the config does not name.

resetTimer of a deadline with nothing to start from now (an enters deadline while the status is in another state, a field deadline whose field holds no date-time), or snoozeTimer of one not started or cancelled; either of a deadline whose until holds.

declaration.name: Numbering
declaration.description: A number a person reads on each instance, set in its create's transaction from a count per namespace and schema: the format prints it, INV-{yyyy}-{seq:4} as INV-2026-0042. The count may run per target of a required, single-valued link and start again each UTC year, so a label is unique within its scope. A refused create takes no number; a delete leaves a gap. Nothing changes a number once set, and a list finds an instance by its label or its number. An instance made before its schema composed Numbering is numbered by assignNumber.

format.description: How a number prints: text with {seq}, or {seq:N} zero-padded to N digits (1 to 10), exactly once, and {yyyy} or {yy}, the UTC year the instance was created in, as often as wanted. No other {...} is allowed.

reset.description: yearly starts the count again at 1 each UTC year, the year the instance was created in; the format must then print the year, {yyyy} or {yy}.

scope.description: Counts per target of a link of the type's Links config, which is required and holds one target: each target's instances are numbered 1, 2, 3, ... of their own.

link.description: The link's name in the type's Links config.

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The instance's number in its count, from 1; absent until it is numbered.

fields.name: label
fields.description: The number as the format prints it, unique within its scope; absent until it is numbered.

operations.name: assignNumber
operations.description: Numbers an instance created before its schema composed Numbering, in the count of the year it was created in, as its create would have. On an instance numbered already it changes nothing and returns its number. A deployment backfills by invoking it in creation order.

label.description: The number as the format prints it.
